title.narrative: Solomon Islands Community Benefits Sharing Project -- Phase 2

description.narrative: The Community Benefit Sharing Pilot Project (CBSP) has been implemented by the Solomon Islands Government (SIG) from 2018 to 2023 with the support of the World Bank. The CBSP pilot aimed to establish a benefit sharing scheme between the Tina River Hydropower Development Project (TRHDP) and the project area communities. The benefits to be shared with these communities are based on an agreed-upon formula between SIG and the dam operator-- Tina Hydro Limited-- that will allocate a portion of the annual revenues from the power generated by the dam for an estimated 30 years after the hydropower plant comes into operation. By enabling the benefits of TRHDP to be shared more broadly with the Malango and Bahomea communities in Malango Ward who may not necessarily receive compensation and royalties from TRHDP, the pilot is expected to reduce the inequality between the members of the core land owning tribes and other residents. The pilot project thereby also served the purpose of sustaining broader community support for the hydropower facility and reducing the risk of disruption to ongoing dam construction.Construction on the TRHDP has been delayed and it is now expected that power-- and therefore revenues to support community benefits-- would not begin to be generated for at least four to five years. Therefore, with the CBSP pilot phase having closed in May 2023, SIG has requested that a phase 2 be prepared to continue to provide benefits to the CBSP target communities. Phase 2 of the Community Benefit Sharing Project (CBSP-2) will build on the pilot CBSP foundation and framework. The Project, like the pilot phase, will be implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) within the Ministry of Mines, Energy, and Rural Electrification (MMERE) and by Solomon Islands Electricity Authority (Solomon Power) for sub-component 2(c), rural electrification (see below). The Project will expand investments started under the pilot in water and electricity access, and include solar where feasible, to ensure that all community members benefit.The project will have four components as follows:-- Component 1: to operationalize the Community Benefits Sharing Fund (CBSF or “Fund”) by establishing the institutional arrangements for the Fund, building the capacity for the oversight and management of the Fund, supporting updates to the Fund Operation Manual and financing community subprojects supporting basic services. The component will consist of two sub-components: 1(a) institutional support to the Fund, and 1(b) small-scale rural infrastructure identified by the communities through a participatory process and screened and approved in accordance with the procedures of the Fund Operations Manual.-- Component 2: to improve access to and use of basic infrastructure and services for the project's target communities. The component will consist of three sub-components: 2(a) rural water supply, 2(b) rural road improvements, and 2(c) rural electrification. Several infrastructure options have been pre-identified under the component and will be confirmed by communities and assessed for final feasibility during the early stages of implementation. Component 2 will include the financing of necessary preparatory activities, such as technical assessments, survey and design and the supervision of the implementation of component 2 civil works. The component would also further inform and test the design, and refine the operational procedures that will be used for component 1(b).-- Component 3: to enhance skills of CBSP community members to increase their knowledge and confidence to participate in the CBSF processes and local economic development activities, and to provide knowledge and skills aimed at income-generating opportunities in both the formal and informal sectors. This would be accomplished through three sub-components that address: 3(a) literacy and numeracy development; 3(b) short technical training focused on existing livelihood activities (such as in agriculture) or linked to work readiness and life-skills training ; and 3(c) employment support services to develop income generation strategies, apply for jobs, obtain references, and so on.-- Component 4: to support project management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E). As with the CBSP Pilot, a Project Management Unit (PMU) will continue to service CBSP-2 and will be co-located with the Project Office of TRHDP, which would continue to provide support on communications, environmental and social standards, gender, citizen engagement and grievance redress. Short-term technical assistance and support through consultant services for specific technical issues will be provided under each of the components described above (i.e., fund advisors, infrastructure engineer, water engineer, skills development specialist etc.). Component 4 will also finance external audits, M&E reports (mid-term and final project review), office equipment (vehicle, furniture, computers), and operating costs necessary to carry out all project-related activities.
to enable Target Communities to benefit from improved access to and use of basic infrastructure and services, and to operationalize the Community Benefit Sharing Fund (CBSF).

title.narrative: Percentage of CBSP community members who feel the CBSP investments reflect their needs

comment.narrative: This is a citizen engagement indicator. Results are based on the first Community Survey completed in September 2025. Survey covered 39 of 80 communities across Bahomea and Malongo areas. The sample size was 480 representing a population of 1,735 community members.

Measured from year 3 of implementation onwards. The score is based on the CBSF achieving a number (10) of key characteristics of a well-functioning benefits sharing scheme. Each characteristic is given a score between 3-5 and is either absolutely achieved (to earn the full score for the characteristic) or relatively achieved (graded from 0 highest score depending on relative achievement). Current score (5/40) reflects: 3/3 (quarterly Board meetings held) + 2/4 member satisfaction (13 percent satisfaction against 20 percent annual target for 2025).

title.narrative: Percentage of CBSF communities which submit a proposal under Component 1b

comment.narrative: Measured as of year 3 of implementation when first cycle of subprojects is released. This indicator will monitor community engagement with the CBSF process. There are approx. 80 communities within the CBSF area. The project anticipates up to 10 proposals in year 3 (when component 1b begins implementation) with the number increasing after that. Not all proposals are expected to be approved and implemented.

title.narrative: Percentage of works contracts completed per annual workplan.

comment.narrative: This will be measured quarterly. Results recorded are cumulative across the year compared with annual workplan.

title.narrative: Timely procurement of project goods, works and services

comment.narrative: Defined as: percentage of contracts planned that are let (signed) within each quarter (average per year).

title.narrative: Number of people who successfully complete training.

comment.narrative: This will be cumulative over the life of the project and will capture all people who successfully complete training under Component 3 activities. The target is based on an expected 600 spaces for literacy/numeracy, plus 720 spaces for technical skills, minus 320 to account for overlap.

title.narrative: Percentage of participants who pass literacy and numeracy training.

comment.narrative: Literacy and numeracy training is tailored to the needs of the participants and will include a pass/fail test to check knowledge.

title.narrative: Percentage of infrastructure subprojects which include climate adaptation measures

comment.narrative: This will be monitored by reviewing subproject designs under components 2 and 1b and identifying which have incorporated relevant climate adaptation measures for the respective sectors (roads & bridges, water, buildings, rural electrification). The current measure refers to water system and road designs.

title.narrative: Percentage of grievances related to project activities which are addressed within a timely manner

comment.narrative: Grievances are tracked through the TRHDP (as done under CBSP) and each grievance is reviewed and directed to the relevant project. Timely means within 3 months. For the quarter ending September 30, 8 out of 9 grievances received have been addressed in a timely manner.

title.narrative: Percentage of members of the Association that are satisfied with the effectiveness of the Fund

comment.narrative: Measured through the Community Survey completed in September 2025. Monitored through a random sample survey of 18+ year old's from the CBSF communities, not just those who are direct beneficiaries of CBSP-2 interventions. Different aspects of effectiveness (communications, engagement, readiness, etc.) were inquired about. Both yes/no questions were asked and a satisfaction scale was used to define satisfaction level.

title.narrative: Percentage of individuals trained who report the training has improved their ability to engage with the CBSF process and in local economic development.

comment.narrative: Results recorded under first Community Survey (September 2025).

title.narrative: Project beneficiaries with improved access to basic services and infrastructure supported under the project (cumulative)

comment.narrative: The number will be calculated by adding: i) the total number of people benefitting from infrastructure investments, and; ii) the number of people who complete training under the project. The target is based on an estimated 4200 beneficiaries under components 1b and 2, and 800 people being trained under component 3. It is probable that beneficiaries will benefit from more than one investment type. Current quarter figure (746) is derived from training graduates (454) + total Antioch village population benefitting from road upgrade (292).

title.narrative: Percentage of HEC employees who are women from CBSP communities.

comment.narrative: HEC has a target of 30% female employees and will aim to have two thirds of that (20% of total employees) coming from the CBSF communities. Based on TRHDP quarterly reports (for Q3 2025, total benefit sharing community employees (M&F) for HEC is 64 of which 11 are women).
